summary.headline: JD Cables H1 FY27 total income rose 38.25% YoY to INR167.89 crore, but net profit of INR12.29 crore (7.32% margin) was roughly flat as EPC drag persisted.
summary.overview: Total income for H1 FY27 grew 38.25% YoY to INR167.89 crore and net profit was INR12.29 crore at a 7.32% margin. Management is exiting the EPC business due to right-of-way and NHAI clearance issues, and is pivoting to cables and conductors. A new Dankuni (West Bengal) facility started in July for conductors and September for cables, with capacity currently at about 50% utilisation. The company proposes to raise up to INR100 crore via QIP or preferential issue, with the use of proceeds still being finalised.

financial_highlights.change: Described by analyst as roughly flat YoY
Roughly doubled vs 31 March (per analyst; not disputed by management)
Management says margins same or higher in H1
Management expects little margin from EPC

segments.name: Cables and conductors
segments.commentary: Order book of about INR300 crore, described as cables-business only. Management guides INR300 crore for H2 FY27 and INR400-500 crore for FY27 (the INR500 crore figure is total company guidance). FY28 guided at INR600-700 crore.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Being exited. Backlog about INR250 crore, expected to shrink, with no further EPC bids. Management expects about INR50 crore in H2 FY27, taking FY27 EPC revenue to about INR110 crore. Work is being subcontracted to two contractors.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 cables and conductors revenue target of about INR300 crore, plus INR40-50 crore from EPC.
FY27 total revenue target of about INR500 crore; the cables and conductors portion is about INR400 crore.
FY28 cables and conductors revenue target of INR600-700 crore.
New plant to reach about 80% utilisation by end of H2 FY27 (assume 80%), and about 85-87% at maximum practical level, implying about INR300 crore annual revenue from the new plant.
Margins guided as similar to current levels, not expanded. EBITDA target of about 13-14%, described as a range management is aiming for.
Order book expected to stay in the INR300-400 crore range; management is not aggressively bidding to limit debt.
capex_capacity: Acquired an industrial facility of about 1.18 lakh sq ft at Dankuni, West Bengal; management says total land is more than 118,000 sq ft.
Within the last year, capex of about INR40-43 crore has been incurred.
Installed capacity will double to a total of 2,800 km; utilisation is about 50% and expected to reach full run-rate from the start of next month.
Conductor division started in July 2026 and cable division in September 2026.
Product pipeline: MVCC and AL-59 conductors from January, HTLS conductors, HT cables; XLPE cables production to start in FY28.
demand_pricing: Management cites strong government T&D spending and data-centre demand for cables and conductors.
Current order book is about INR300 crore, with multi-year contracts drawn down on utility call-off schedules.
Top five customers are about 40-50% of revenue (approximate, to be confirmed).
Supply presence across more than 15 states, with Punjab, Himachal, MP, Chhattisgarh and the South now active. Maharashtra and UP are targeted next.
Competition: management says Ultratech/Birla's entry is in retail house-wiring, which JD Cables has not entered, and that its own products are cheaper and it offers faster delivery.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crore fund raise be allocated and what ROE or ROCE is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Use is for plant and machinery, land and working capital. Management has not yet calculated the expected return and will revert later.

qa_highlights.question: Debt has nearly doubled and finance cost has surged over 100% HoH. What is the cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of borrowing is 8-9%, with no loans at 15% or higher. The increase is attributed to short-term borrowings used to fund about INR40-43 crore of capex and working capital.

qa_highlights.question: How much EPC revenue will be booked in FY27, and why are margins lower?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore is done to date and INR50 crore is expected in H2, so about INR110 crore for FY27. The margin drag is blamed on right-of-way and NHAI clearance issues, and the decision to exit EPC.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 margins expand by 200-250 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects margins similar to current levels, with cables PAT margin at about 8-9% and EPC margin low.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any contingent liabilities or disputes from the EPC business?
Why is the fund raise being done, and is it QIP or preferential?
qa_highlights.answer: The raise is for expansion and working capital, via QIP or preferential issue. Discussions are ongoing and the structure is not finalised.

risks_watch: EPC exit execution: whether the backlog of about INR250 crore can be subcontracted without losses or disputes.
Debt of about INR118 crore and finance cost up more than 100% HoH; watch debt reduction after the INR100 crore fund raise.
Ramp-up of the new Dankuni plant from about 50% toward 80% by end-H2 and whether H2 revenue of about INR300 crore is met.
Margin trajectory: management guides flat margins, which conflicts with analyst expectations of H2 expansion.
Customer concentration: top five customers about 40-50% of revenue.
Inconsistent guidance: FY27 EPC revenue estimates ranged from INR110 crore to INR200 crore on the call, and the total FY27 target was stated as INR500 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity growth, but evasive or vague on specifics: return on the fund raise, margin outlook, the EPC backlog figure, and the purpose of the raise. Several answers were corrected or walked back during the call, including the FY27 revenue target and the order-book trajectory.
key_quotes: So, there is no doubt there is a huge demand for cables and conductors.
Average cost, sir, is 8% to 9%, sir.
At the end of H2, ma'am, we are expecting around 80% to 85% capacity.
If we aggressively bid, debt will certainly increase further only.

adds.what: Dankuni (West Bengal) facility, ~1.18 lakh sq ft, conductors and cables; installed capacity to double to 2,800 km

growth.why: Guides FY27 total revenue ~INR500 crore (cables ~INR400 crore) and FY28 cables INR600-700 crore, backed by a ~INR300 crore cables order book and the Dankuni plant doubling capacity to 2,800 km, though utilisation is only 50% today and EPC is being exited.

quality.why: H1 FY27 total income rose 38.25% YoY to INR167.89 crore, but the brief does not state the driver split between volume, price or mix, and names no one-off items in the growth; net profit was roughly flat, with EPC drag and higher finance costs (up over 100% HoH) weighing on earnings rather than revenue growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides margins flat at current levels (cables PAT 8-9%, EPC margin low), with EBITDA target of 13-14%, so the analyst-expected 200-250 bps H2 expansion is not supported.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dankuni facility already commissioned (conductors July 2026, cables September 2026), taking installed capacity to 2,800 km, a doubling; utilisation is only 50% today.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Cables and conductors revenue guided to about INR300 crore in H2 FY27 and INR600-700 crore in FY28, backed by an INR300 crore order book and the new plant ramping from 50% toward 80-85% by end-H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 50% so the near-term need is limited, but the proposed INR100 crore QIP or preferential raise for plant, machinery, land and working capital points to further capex, with use of proceeds still being finalised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance has been cut or walked back during the call: EPC H2 revenue cut to INR40-50 crore, FY27 total target stated inconsistently, and the order book may shrink to INR250 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 total target of about INR500 crore and H2 cables revenue of INR300 crore depend on ramping the new plant from 50% to 80-85% and on order book holding at INR300-400 crore, and EPC backlog of about INR250 crore is being subcontracted with execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management lists MVCC and AL-59 conductors from January, HTLS conductors, HT cables, and XLPE cables production starting in FY28.

rows.label: EPC business exit
rows.why: Management is exiting EPC with no further bids; backlog of about INR250 crore is being subcontracted to two contractors and H2 FY27 EPC revenue is expected at INR40-50 crore, which shifts mix toward cables at 8-9% PAT margin.

rows.label: Debt reduction after fund raise
rows.why: Debt is about INR118 crore, roughly doubled since 31 March, with finance cost up over 100% HoH at 8-9% average borrowing cost; INR100 crore QIP or preferential issue could reduce short-term borrowings, but use of proceeds and structure are not finalised.

rows.label: Order book trajectory
rows.why: Management guides order book at INR300-400 crore by FY27 end, though it was walked back to possibly INR250 crore; not aggressively bidding to limit debt, and top five customers are 40-50% of revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on T&D and data-centre demand, capacity doubling and product pipeline, but vague on the fund raise return, margin outlook, EPC backlog and order book, with several figures corrected during the call; analysts pushed on debt doubling, finance cost surge, and margin expansion e
